However, due to occlusion and signal miss, LiDAR point clouds are in practice 2.5D as they cover only partial underlying shapes, which poses a fundamental challenge to 3D perception.

To tackle the challenge, we present a novel LiDAR-based 3D object detection model, dubbed Behind the Curtain Detector (BtcDet), which learns the object shape priors and estimates the complete object shapes that are partially occluded (curtained) in point clouds.

In this paper, we propose Behind the Curtain Detector (BtcDet).
We propose to voxelize the point cloud using an evenly spaced spherical grid so that the occluded regions can be accurately formed by the spherical voxels behind any LiDAR point.
